note: Pirelli donated the land of its former sports and social club to Burton Albion in return for naming rights; the club built the £7.2m stadium in 2005. Sources describe the stadium as owned by the club; no later sale or leaseback found, but freehold title not confirmed by a primary source.

lease_note: Short-term licence extended from June 2026 by at least one year, with an option for one more year (to June 2028 at most); no further extensions possible
note: Former club owner Firoz Kassam kept the stadium through his Firoka Group when he sold the club, so Oxford United are licensees. The club won final approval for a new 16,000-seat stadium at the Triangle near Kidlington in February 2026, though a legal challenge was launched in 2026.

lease_note: 250-year lease agreed in principle 2022, completion targeted by end of April 2024 (end year approximate)
note: Stockport Council bought Edgeley Park for £2m in 2015 from Cheshire Sport Promotions and leased it back to the club. Under owner Mark Stott the club agreed a 250-year lease in 2022, with the council keeping the freehold.
Exeter City Council owns the land under St James Park and leases it to the supporter-owned club; a new 25-year lease was agreed in 2020.

lease_note: Club holds a long leasehold on the stadium (2019 administration sale particulars); length and freeholder not found
note: The 2019 administration sale particulars describe the stadium as a long leasehold venue, so the club does not hold the freehold outright. The Middlebrook site was developed as a partnership of Orbit Developments, Bolton Wanderers and Bolton Council, but no source names the current freeholder.

Barnet first occupied The Hive under a lease from the London Borough of Harrow, then bought the freehold from Harrow for about £2m in 2018. Some sources say Kleanthous personally bought it; the most specific report says the club owns it, but whether a separate Kleanthous company holds title is not confirmed.

lease_note: 150-year lease from December 2003, held by County Developments Northampton Ltd (club subsidiary)
note: The council (formerly Northampton Borough Council, now West Northamptonshire Council) owns the stadium freehold; the club's subsidiary CDNL holds a 150-year lease. In 2025 the council accepted a £2m bid from CDNL for adjacent development land, linked to finishing the East Stand.

The club built the ground (formerly New Meadow) and moved there in 2007 under chairman Roland Wycherley; sources list the club as owner. Separately, Wycherley's training-ground land was transferred to the club in exchange for shares.

Holker Street was sold for £410,000 to Northern Improvements, a company linked to former chairman Stephen Vaughan; after a 1998-2002 legal battle the sale was deemed improper and the new members' company bought the ground from the liquidator in 2002. Sources list the club as owner.

Eastleigh have played at Ten Acres since 1957 and the ground was redeveloped under Stewart Donald from 2010. Reference sources list the club as owner, but no source confirms freehold title or rules out a council lease.

owner_name: The New Show Ground Community Interest Company
lease_note: Club holds a lease from the CIC; term not found
note: Former chairman Peter Swann kept Glanford Park through Coolsilk Property and Investment and gave the club notice to pay £3m or quit, leading to a court dispute. On 29 November 2023 a not-for-profit CIC set up by barrister Tahina Akther bought the ground, mainly with Town Deal Fund money via North Lincolnshire Council, and leases it to the club.

Reference sources list Harrogate Town AFC as owner of Wetherby Road, its home since 1920. One local opinion piece speaks of the club 'leasing land on Wetherby Road', so a council lease of part or all of the site cannot be ruled out.

Buxton have played at the Silverlands since 1884, on a field first owned by the club's first captain. A fan-site review of the club's accounts says Buxton own their ground, valued at about £600k on the balance sheet.

Worthing have played at Woodside Road since 1901 and owner George Dowell has funded a 3G pitch and stand expansion approved by Worthing Borough Council in April 2024. No source found that says who holds the freehold.

lease_note: Ground lease from the council; term not found
note: After reforming in 1989 the club moved in 1993 to a council-chosen former tree nursery at Meadow Lane, built with council money and volunteer work. Bedford Borough Council's June 2024 land register lists the Bedford Town FC ground as council freehold, ground leasehold.

lease_note: 35-year lease approved June 2024 (replacing earlier 15-year peppercorn lease); end year approximate
note: Chorley Council bought Victory Park when Ken Wright and Graham Watkinson took over the club's shares, and granted a 15-year peppercorn lease. In June 2024 the council approved a new 35-year lease so the club can seek larger grants for ground improvements.

lease_note: Club operates the ground under an arrangement with the council; terms not found
note: Crabble Athletic Ground was bought for public use in 1902 and is owned by Dover District Council; Dover Athletic operate it. No current lease details found.

owner_name: London Borough of Richmond upon Thames
lease_note: Council gave notice (2023) of intent to grant a stadium lease for up to 125 years plus a licence for practice pitch and car park; completion not confirmed
note: The Beveree is council open space in Hampton. Richmond Council published notice of its intention to grant the club a lease of the 1.2-hectare stadium for up to 125 years, linked to approved redevelopment plans.

Researched phoenix club Macclesfield FC. After Macclesfield Town was wound up in September 2020, local businessman Robert Smethurst bought Moss Rose for about £500,000 from the liquidators and set up Macclesfield FC to play there; reports say Smethurst bought it, but it is not confirmed whether title sits with him, a separate company or the club company.

lease_note: Club operates the ground; lease terms not found
note: Researched phoenix club Merthyr Town (Merthyr Tydfil FC was dissolved in 2010). Penydarren Park is owned by Merthyr Tydfil County Borough Council and operated by Merthyr Town; a 3G pitch was added in 2014 with community fund money.

Hemel Hempstead Town moved into Hemel Hempstead United's Vauxhall Road ground in 1972; the land was once part of Cox Pond Farm bought by Arthur Brock in the 1930s. No source found that says who holds the freehold now.

lease_note: Lease taken over by Salisbury FC in early 2015; term not found
note: Researched phoenix club Salisbury FC (Salisbury City was dissolved in 2014). The stadium is owned by the estate of former chairman Raymond McEnhill, which had proposed selling the land for development before granting the new club a lease in 2015.

lease_note: Long lease from the council; term not found
note: Sefton Council holds the freehold of Haig Avenue and Southport FC is a long leaseholder. The arrangement dates from 1919, when the Southport Education Committee took over the lease and granted one to the club.

lease_note: Lease runs to 2081; talks in 2025 to reset it to 125 years
note: Torbay Council owns the Plainmoor freehold and leases it to Torquay United; a planned club purchase of the freehold was postponed in 2017 and the council says the freehold will stay in its ownership. In 2025 the club reported advanced talks to reset the lease to 125 years.

ground: Sandy Lane (Windsor Food Park / Windsor Foodservice Stadium)
lease_note: Council freehold; head lease held by Peter Whitehead (bought 2011, owner of Worksop Parramore); Worksop Town were sub-tenants on short leases (12 months plus option of 2 years in 2016)
note: Worksop Town were evicted from Sandy Lane in 2008 by leaseholder 1861 Leisure and played elsewhere until Peter Whitehead bought the lease in 2011 and let them return. The council owns the freehold and said it could not justify buying back the lease; no newer source found on the current head lease.
Anstey Nomads have played at Cropston Road since forming in 1946 and received Football Stadia Improvement Fund grants for it. No source found that says who holds the freehold.

lease_note: Lease from the council; term not found
note: Avro moved to the council-owned Whitebank Stadium in 2017 after Oldham Council earmarked their old ground for housing, and were granted a lease; the ground was redeveloped with a 3G pitch and floodlights and a permanent expansion was later approved.

owner_name: Bath City FC (majority-owned by Bath City Supporters' Society)
note: Bath City have played at Twerton Park since 1932; the club became community-owned in 2017 when the Supporters' Society bought a majority of shares, and reports describe Twerton Park as community-owned with it. The club signed an MoU with Greenacre Capital to redevelop the ground with student housing; freehold title not confirmed by a primary source.

lease_note: Tenant of the council; terms not found
note: Brentwood Town moved to the council's Brentwood Centre site in October 1993 with council help; reports describe council and club as landlord and tenant in talks over a football hub there. A 3G pitch was laid in 2024.
